sentences.text:
The petitioner vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seeks quashing of FIR No.567/2021 dated 26.07.2021 registered under Sections 406/498A/34 IPC at P.S. Dabri, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Mutual Agreement dated 22.05.2023 arrived at between the parties.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Mutual Agreement dated 22.05.2023 [Annexure-P3] and is also supported by affidavits of the petitioner and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3.
Petitioner as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/10/2023 at 00:24:53 4.
Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.

Respondent no.2 confirms that the Ajay Rajput vs The State Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45894731/
1 petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 15.07.2023.

sentences.text: She further affirms the Mutual Agreement dated 22.05.2023 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.
